slides.title: Cryptographic and Password Attacks
points: Distinguish cryptographic attacks from password attacks by what the attacker is weakening or varying.
Security+ Objective 2.4: given a scenario, analyze indicators of malicious activity.

slides.title: Downgrade Attack
slides.teach: Forces systems to use an older or weaker protocol, cipher, or security mode.

course.learn: Forces systems to use an older or weaker protocol, cipher, or security mode.

breakdown.explanation: Make both sides fall back to weaker security.

course.why: Older modes may contain known weaknesses.
course.example: A connection is forced from a modern protocol to a legacy one.
course.check_q: Which attack forces weaker protocol negotiation?

slides.title: Collision Attack
slides.teach: Attempts to find two different inputs that produce the same hash output.

course.learn: Attempts to find two different inputs that produce the same hash output.
course.why: Collisions weaken assumptions that a digest uniquely represents content.
course.example: Two different files produce the same hash.
course.check_q: Which attack finds two different inputs with the same hash?

slides.title: Birthday Attack
slides.teach: Uses probability properties to find hash collisions faster than naive exhaustive comparison.

course.learn: Uses probability properties to find hash collisions faster than naive exhaustive comparison.

breakdown.explanation: Exploit birthday-paradox probability to find a collision.

course.why: Collisions become likely sooner than full keyspace intuition suggests.
course.example: An attacker searches for any two inputs sharing a digest.

slides.title: Password Spraying
slides.teach: Tries a small number of common passwords across many accounts.

course.learn: Tries a small number of common passwords across many accounts.
course.example: Winter2026! is tried once against hundreds of users.
course.check_q: Which attack tries one common password across many accounts?

slides.title: Brute Force
slides.teach: Systematically tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.

course.learn: Systematically tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.

breakdown.explanation: Many guesses against one account, Key-space search

course.why: Weak or short secrets may eventually be discovered.
course.example: Thousands of password candidates are attempted against one account.
course.check_q: Which attack systematically tries many candidates?

blocks.title: Know what the attacker is varying
items: The attacker makes both sides use weaker protections.
Example: A connection falls back to a legacy protocol.
Different inputs share one hash → COLLISION
Distinct data produces the same digest.
Example: Two files share one hash value.
Example: A collision is found sooner than naive search suggests.
One common password across many users → SPRAYING
Example: Winter2026! is tried once against hundreds of users.
Many guesses against target → BRUTE FORCE
Candidates are tried repeatedly until one succeeds.
Example: Thousands of passwords target one account.
blocks.example: Memory: Downgrade = weaker · Collision = same hash · Birthday = collision probability · Spray = few/many · Brute force = many guesses.

questions.q: An attacker forces two systems to negotiate an older, weaker protocol. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: A downgrade attack forces use of weaker security settings.

questions.q: Two different files are crafted to produce the same hash. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: A collision occurs when different inputs produce the same hash output.

questions.q: An attacker exploits birthday-paradox probability to find any two inputs with the same hash. Which attack is this?
Winter2026! is tried once against hundreds of accounts. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: Password spraying uses a few common passwords across many accounts.

questions.q: Thousands of password guesses are attempted against one administrator account. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: Brute force repeatedly tries many candidates against a target.
